art.subject: Plumbeous Water Redstart (Rhyacornis fuliginosa), adult male: entire head and body dark slate-blue (plumbeous), slightly paler on the belly; wings dark brownish-grey; rump, uppertail coverts, undertail coverts and the whole tail deep chestnut-rufous. Bill short and black; dark eye; legs dark brown to blackish. The female, if shown, is blue-grey above, white below with dense grey scaling, with white spots on the wing-coverts and a white base to the tail.
art.pose: standing on a wet boulder in a stream, rufous tail fanned and flicked, side view
art.scene: fast, clear mountain stream with mossy boulders in a Korean valley in spring; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view standing on a wet boulder with the tail fanned: slaty-blue head, body and underparts, darker blackish wings, chestnut rump, uppertail coverts, undertail coverts and whole tail, short black bill, dark legs

adult female, side view standing on a boulder with the tail fanned: slaty-grey head and upperparts, browner wings with two rows of small white spots, underparts scaled grey and white, white rump and undertail coverts, brown tail with white bases to the outer feathers
art.build: Small, compact chat, a little smaller than a sparrow, round-bodied with a short neck. Bill short, thin and straight. Legs fairly long, slender, dark. Short wings; tail short to medium, square-ended, constantly fanned open and wagged up and down or flicked sideways. Perches on wet boulders in rushing water, making short sallies after insects.
avoid: Do not paint a white cap or a black-and-chestnut body; that is White-capped Water Redstart (Phoenicurus leucocephalus).
Do not paint orange underparts or a white wing patch (Daurian Redstart).
Do not give the male any white in the tail; the whole tail is chestnut-rufous.
